title: Contribution flow, review checklist, and deprecation roadmap for component library
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Establish a pragmatic contribution flow and unambiguous deprecation roadmap for the design system (tokens, buttons, tables, charts) that reduces churn, protects stability for product teams, and speeds review cycles. This ticket collects a single-source guidance doc + review checklist + example RFC template + deprecation timeline and signals for retiring components or tokens. It must cover designer and engineer responsibilities, automated checks, required artifacts, and communication cadence for end users (storybook, changelog, Slack/Docs).
acceptance_criteria: A single contributor-facing guideline doc exists in Confluence and is linked from the repo README
A pull request checklist (lintable) with required items (design spec, accessibility, token usage, visual diff) is added to the template
An RFC template for breaking or behavioral changes is published and a gate in PRs references it
Deprecation policy defines timelines (soft deprecation, telemetry window, hard removal), and a sample deprecation announcement workflow
At least two components (one visual: Button v2, one layout: Table responsive) have run through the new flow and documented lessons learned
tasks: Draft Confluence doc: contribution flow and responsibilities (design/engineering/PM)
Create PR template + CI job to enforce checklist items (visual regression, a11y, token usage)
Draft RFC template and publish as repository template and Confluence starter
Define telemetry events for usage of tokens/components and add to tracking plan (collaborate with Analytics)
Write deprecation playbook with examples and timeline macros
Run pilot with Button v2 and Table responsive rework; collect feedback
Announce policy to product teams and schedule office hours for migration questions
decision_log: 2026-01-27 — Decision: Use 3-stage deprecation (announce -> supported-but-deprecated -> removal). Chosen timeline defaults: 90 days announce, 180 days supported-deprecated, 360 days removal for visual API changes — Sofia M., Liam O'Connor (Engineering)

2026-02-10 — Decision: Mandatory artifacts for any component change: design spec (Figma link), implementation PR, visual regression screenshots, a11y report, migration notes. Exception process required for hotfixes — Asha P., Priya Banerjee (Design Ops)

2026-02-25 — Decision: Adopt semantic component versioning in CHANGELOG: patch/non-behavior changes, minor/opt-in feature changes, major/behavioral or API changes that require RFC — Engineering + Design agreed
review_checklist: Design: link to canonical Figma frame(s) and spec with tokens called out
Tokens: confirm new token usage or mapping; avoid duplicate tokens; document token migration mapping
Visuals: run visual-regression; include before/after snapshots and threshold explanation
Accessibility: axe report + keyboard/screenreader checks; contrast ratio for tokens used in text/background
API/props: document stable public props; mark experimental props in docs
Docs: update Storybook stories, migration guide, and changelog entry
Performance: include notes if component affects render/paint (large tables/charts), and any batching or virtualization required
Telemetry: add usage event or flag to indicate adoption and to monitor slow migration
Compatibility: list known product pages where component is used; add integration test target if high-risk
Backwards compatibility: provide a fallback or feature flag for staged rollout
deprecation_policy_summary: When a token or component is slated for removal the system follows: (1) Announcement (at least 90 days) with migration docs; (2) Supported-but-deprecated phase (typically 180 days) where behavior remains but deprecation warnings are surfaced in console/docs and telemetry is collected; (3) Removal after a minimum of 360 days for breaking changes unless emergency security/bug fixes require acceleration. For non-breaking cosmetic consolidations (token merges) timeline may be shorter (60/120/180) with migration tooling provided. All deprecations require an RFC and a documented migration path and must be listed in the public CHANGELOG and a central Deprecation Dashboard.
